conviction_note: The stock trades on the FY guide: a cut cost -27% in Nov 2025 and -38% in May 2026, and a reiteration gained +19% in Aug 2026. The FY26 guide needs H2 adj EBITDA of $28.3-33.3m against $16.7m in H1. The closest SEO-led US peer (Catena) printed NA revenue -29% in Q3, and the 3.0x leverage covenant is getting tight, so a cut or trim is the likely outcome. But the stock is -59% since the last print and sits at about 3x EV on guided EBITDA, so much of a cut is priced, and a held guide would squeeze it. The result is p_up 46 on an abs move of 26. The findings sum (-2.8) is a little more negative than the scaled number (-2.1) because the expectations finding offsets only part of the fundamental negatives.

expectations.real_bar: The stock rises if Q3 adj EBITDA shows the cost-savings ramp (roughly $10m+), any guide cut is modest and keeps leverage under the 3.0x covenant, and there is no equity raise or share-settled earnout. A held FY guide would be well above the real bar. A deep cut combined with a covenant amendment or dilution is below it.

next_guide.basis: H1 adj EBITDA was $16.7m ($9.0m + $7.7m), so the guide needs $28.3-33.3m in H2, and H2 revenue of $86.8-91.8m (+2% to +7.5% YoY) against Q2's -5% YoY. The closest SEO-led US affiliate peer (Catena) pre-announced Q3 NA revenue -29% on AI search, and DraftKings plans lower 2027 marketing. That points to a cut or a low-end/trim. Offsets: NA marketing +63% in Q2, $6.5m of H2 cost savings, and DraftKings' heavy Q3 acquisition spend.

findings.finding: The FY26 guide ($45-50m adj EBITDA, $165-170m revenue) needs H2 adj EBITDA of $28.3-33.3m, i.e. about $14-17m a quarter, against Q2's $7.7m and Q1's $9.0m. H2 revenue must be $86.8-91.8m (+2% to +7.5% YoY vs H2 2025's $85.4m) after Q2 printed -5% YoY. Street FY revenue sits at $165.4m, the bottom of the range, so the street already leans to the low end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name trades on the FY guide: cut on 2025-11-13 -27%, cut on 2026-05-14 -38%, reiterated on 2026-08-13 +19%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The -59% since the last print and an EV of about 3x guided EBITDA show the market has already discounted a cut, while the published consensus and the $4.43 targets still sit on the guide. What is not priced is the size: if the cut takes EBITDA to the high $30m's, covenant headroom (see the covenant finding) becomes the issue, not the cut itself.

findings.finding: Catena Media, a US-focused SEO/CPA casino and sports affiliate (97% of revenue from North America), pre-announced on 2026-10-19 Q3 2026 revenue -29% to EUR 8.3m and adj EBITDA -75% to EUR 0.7m. It blamed AI-driven search changes and lower operator marketing spend, and dropped its 2026 growth target. The final report on 2026-11-10 showed NA revenue -29% to EUR 7.9m.
findings.link: Same business model and channel as GRSD's marketing segment: organic-search affiliate sites earning CPA from US online casino and sportsbook operators. GRSD marketing was $26.5m of $37.8m Q2 revenue (70%), and its declines came from 'organic search and markets outside North America'. Not a counterparty.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Search-driven marketing misses led to the guide cuts: Nov 2025 (spam sites in search, -27%) and May 2026 (weak organic search, -38%).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. GRSD fell about 25% in the month after (to $1.17 on 2026-10-26) and on down to $0.74. GRSD's NA marketing grew +63% YoY in Q2 on partner and paid channels, so the transmission is partial and the market may not separate the two.
findings.independence: Catena's own interim report release, 2026-11-10 (https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/a-disappointing-quarter-as-search-pressures-weigh-on-revenue). Better Collective (separate finding) points the other way for NA.

findings.link: Affiliate and sports media business paid by the same US operators. BC's NA growth credited revenue-share, prediction markets and talent-led media, which are less SEO-driven than GRSD's model. The share of overlapping clients is not stated.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history for this line.

findings.finding: Covenant and obligations: the Wells Fargo facility caps leverage at 3.00x, with a fixed-charge minimum of 1.25x and a $15.0m minimum liquidity. Borrowings were $122.3m at 30 June against cash of $8.8m and total liquidity of $33.3m, with net current liabilities of $23.1m. A further $26.5m of OddsJam deferred consideration is now current (due about April 2027, up to 70% settleable in shares), plus Spotlight.Vegas earnouts of up to $11m in April 2027. LTM adj EBITDA is about $45.1m (Q3'25 $13.0m + Q4'25 about $15.4m + Q1'26 $9.0m + Q2'26 $7.7m), so gross leverage is about 2.7x. If Q3'26 EBITDA comes in below about $9.6m in place of Q3'25's $13.0m, gross leverage passes 3.0x unless covenant EBITDA adds back restructuring.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for this line. The company has had no covenant event or equity raise since its IPO.
findings.why_not_priced: Asked what the money buys: it pays for past acquisitions (OddsJam, Spotlight), not a visible ramp, so the sign is negative. A $26m market cap against $122m of debt says equity holders already fear dilution. What is not priced is the specific trigger: a share-settled earnout at $0.74 (about $18.5m / $0.74 = about 25m shares against 35.6m outstanding) or a covenant amendment announced with the print. A clean statement of headroom would relieve that fear, hence the positive high end.
findings.independence: Covenant terms are in the Q1 2026 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001839799/000183979926000101/q12026quarterlyfinancials.htm). The leverage path is my own arithmetic, an inference. The FY25 Q4 EBITDA is derived from the FY25 total of $58.0m in the 20-F.

outside_window.finding: $26.5m of OddsJam deferred consideration and up to $11m of Spotlight.Vegas earnout fall due in April 2027. Up to 70% of the OddsJam 2026 amount can be settled in shares, which would be heavily dilutive at $0.74. The settlement decision itself lands in 2027; any statement of intent with the print is captured in the covenant finding.
The share price has been below $1 since about early November. A Nasdaq minimum-bid deficiency notice needs 30 consecutive business days below $1, so it lands after the window.

baseline_tension: There is no skew and no implied move. The evidence leans negative (guide arithmetic, the SEO peer, covenant tightness), which agrees with the -42% run-up, so much of it is priced. The run-up itself makes a held guide the larger surprise, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 'documents beat inference, not covenant arithmetic': covenant breach path -2.5 to -1.5. The covenant terms are documented; the breach is my inference.

Lesson 5 (proxy vs broader series): the Catena SEO proxy is contradicted in part by Better Collective's NA +28% and GRSD's own NA marketing +63%, so -2.0 to -1.5. The Q3 revenue run-rate inference goes -1.5 to -1.0.
Lesson 3 / pessimism artefact: the guide finding goes -3.0 to -2.5 because its own text says the cut is mostly priced. DraftKings 2027 goes -1.0 to -0.8. p_up moves 45 to 46.
'Rebuild history from confirmed releases': the reaction history is rebuilt (-27, -38, +19) and abs_move set to 26 from 25.
Lesson 6: two consensus sources agree on Q3 revenue ($41.5m / $42.0m), so the revenue findings are not capped; EPS is disputed and not used.
Left standing: expectations +2.5, BC +0.5, DraftKings Q3 +1.0, insider, short interest, Rollcard 0.
